method: real task-like questions over the domain fixtures. Each task labels the fact set a correct answer must contain (the ImpactCandidate.qualified_name forms measured in lf-0135 — same names, same seeds). Arms: (a) no-atlas = iterative literal grep+read simulation over the fixture tree; (b) pack-only = real DomainContextEngine.build_domain pack (budget 4000); (c) atlas+search = real `impact symbol` JSON and real `domains entities/lineage` calls. Proxy only — no LLM/agent harness exists (declared NOT RUN).

tasks.question: what breaks if table landing.orders changes
tasks.notes: 10 verified blast nodes over a 5-file SQL warehouse — the pack/impact must beat read-everything in both tokens and queries.

tasks.question: what breaks if Iceberg table lake.db.orders changes
tasks.notes: 4 dependents of the catalog table (archive + 2 statements + the glue job) spread across a 30-file repo — grep must read many files to confirm.

tasks.question: what breaks if table staging.orders (read by spark jobs) changes
tasks.notes: 10 blast nodes across two jobs — including the job entities themselves (reachable only via CONTAINS, invisible to data-flow lineage).

tasks.question: what breaks if FastAPI route GET /pets/ is removed
tasks.notes: Route removal hits the router aggregate + handler symbol + module + file — the code-symbol facts come through the DEFINES domain->code bridge.

tasks.question: what breaks if terraform module network changes
tasks.notes: Two provisioned resources inside the module — reachable via coupled PROVISIONS.

tasks.question: what breaks if IAM role aws_iam_role.glue is removed
tasks.notes: 16 of 24 terraform entities — the widest blast in the corpus; no-atlas has to read nearly every .tf file.

tasks.question: what breaks if the reusable workflow Reusable Checks changes
tasks.notes: Caller job + its needs-chain (release -> deploy) + workflow aggregate — 4 nodes over 4 workflow files.

tasks.question: what breaks if the sql-declared staging.orders changes (cross-adapter consumers)
tasks.notes: Blast crosses the REFERENCES identity bridge into the pyspark view of the same table — grep has no notion of the identity link but finds it by name.

tasks.question: who calls endpoint POST /v1/pets
tasks.notes: Single-fact who-calls: the resolved Python caller (web.client.loadPets stays ambiguous — deliberately not a fact).
